APA title case

Source: R/apa-title-case.R
apa_title_case.Rd

Capitalization is only ever ADDED, never removed – except for the one deliberate exception below. The later branch that force-capitalizes a word's first letter (`substr(w,1,1) <- toupper(...)`) can never itself destroy an all-caps acronym: an acronym already starts uppercase, so that branch is a no-op on it regardless of whether the guard below runs. What the guard actually protects is different and easy to miss: an acronym that COLLIDES, case-insensitively, with an entry in `APA_TITLE_LOWERCASE` – OR (odds ratio), AS (anxiety sensitivity), AN (anorexia nervosa), SO (significant other), VIA (Values in Action) are all real column names that are also minor words. Without the guard, `tolower(w) "or", "as", "an", "so", "via", silently destroying the acronym. See `test-apa-title-case.R`, "an acronym that collides with a minor word survives", which is the only test in the suite that can observe this guard failing. Function words are still lowercased even when the author capitalized them, because a strict never-downcase rule would leave "Score For Test" and break the very rule being applied – and a function word is never an acronym, so that is safe.

Usage

apa_title_case(x)
